title: Deinococcus radiodurans-derived membrane vesicles protect HaCaT cells against oxidative stress
author: Han, Song, et al.
materials: Deinococcus radiodurans strains were grown at 30 °C for 72 h under static conditions for isolation and purification of the R1-MVs. Briefly, after culturing in TGY broth for 72 h, the bacteria-free culture supernatants were harvested by centrifugation (10,000 × g, 30 min, 4 °C). The supernatant was filtered through a 0.45 μm bottle-top vacuum filter system (Corning, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany) using a Minimate™ tangential flow filtration (TFF) system with an Omega™ 300 K membrane capsule (Pall Scientific, NY, USA). The R1-EV pellets were harvested by ultracentrifugation (100,000 × g, 2 h, 4 °C), washed in sterile phosphate buffer saline (PBS; pH 7.4), and then purified by centrifugation using Optiprep density gradient medium (Sigma, #D1556, Steinheim, Germany). The R1-MVs were purified by ultracentrifugation (18 h, 170,000 × g, 4 °C; under no brake condition) in a discontinuous 60% Optiprep density gradient medium [step gradient ranging from 10 to 60% (w/v)]. The final MV pellet was resuspended in PBS and stored at − 80 °C. The protein content of R1-MVs was assessed using a bicinchoninic acid (BCA) protein assay kit (Thermo Scientific Pierce, Rockford, IL, USA) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.

HaCaT cells were seeded in a 6-well plate and treated with H2O2 (0.3 mM) in the presence or absence of R1-MVs (10 and 30 μg/mL). Cytosolic and nuclear proteins were extracted using cell lysis buffer (RIPA buffer, Pierce, Rockford, IL, USA) and the CelLytic NuCLEAR Extraction Kit (Sigma-Aldrich), respectively. Protein concentration was measured using the BCA protein assay. Proteins were isolated using 10% SDS–PAGE and electrically transferred to polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) membranes. The membranes were blocked with 5% skim milk and incubated with the respective primary antibodies (1:1000 dilution; anti-Bcl-2, anti-Bax, anti-cytochrome C, anti-cleaved-caspase 3, anti-cleaved-caspase 8, anti-cleaved-caspase 9, anti-PARP, anti-p38, anti-ERK, anti-JNK, anti-p38, phosphorylated (p)-ERK, p-JNK, p-p38, Nrf2, β-actin, and anti-α-tubulin antibodies) overnight at 4 °C. Thereafter, the membranes were incubated with an HRP-conjugated secondary antibody (anti-rabbit Ab, 1:5000 dilution) for 1 h at RT. Proteins were visualized using an electrochemiluminescence advance kit (Millipore, Merck KGaA, Darmstadt, Germany). Primary and secondary antibodies were purchased from Cell Signaling Technology (Danvers, MA, USA) and Calbiochem (San Diego, CA, USA), respectively.

steps.title: Grow D. radiodurans and harvest supernatant
steps.instruction: Incubate Deinococcus radiodurans in TGY broth at 30 °C under static conditions for 72 h; then centrifuge the culture at 10,000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C to obtain bacteria‑free supernatant.

steps.title: Filter supernatant and pellet extracellular vesicles
steps.instruction: Pass the supernatant through a 0.45 µm bottle‑top vacuum filter (Corning, Merck KGaA) using a Minimate™ tangential flow filtration system with an Omega™ 300 K membrane capsule (Pall Scientific); subsequently ultracentrifuge the filtrate at 100,000 × g for 2 h at 4 °C to pellet R1‑EVs.

steps.title: Purify vesicles by OptiPrep gradient
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet in sterile PBS (pH 7.4); layer it onto a discontinuous OptiPrep density gradient (Sigma #D1556) ranging from 10 % to 60 % (w/v) with a final 60 % step; ultracentrifuge at 170,000 × g for 18 h at 4 °C without brake; collect the R1‑MV band, resuspend in PBS, and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Quantify protein content of R1‑MVs
steps.instruction: Determine the protein concentration of the resuspended vesicles using a bicinchoninic acid (BCA) protein assay kit (Thermo Scientific Pierce) following the manufacturer’s protocol.

steps.title: Measure vesicle size distribution
steps.instruction: Analyze the average diameter of R1‑MVs by dynamic light scattering (DLS) (average ≈ 300 nm); confirm size range (290–330 nm) using transmission electron microscopy (TEM, scale bar = 500 nm) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM, scale bar = 200 nm).

steps.title: Assess antioxidant activity of R1‑MVs
steps.instruction: Perform DPPH and FRAP assays with R1‑MVs at concentrations of 0.25–2 mg mL⁻¹ to evaluate dose‑dependent radical scavenging and ferric‑reducing abilities.

steps.title: Culture HaCaT keratinocyte cells
steps.instruction: Maintain HaCaT cells (Lonza/Korean Cell Line Bank) in Dulbecco’s Modified Eagle’s Medium (DMEM, Biowest) supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum (Biowest) and 1 % penicillin‑streptomycin (GIBCO) at 37 °C in a humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Treat cells for western blot analysis
steps.instruction: Seed HaCaT cells in 6‑well plates; add H₂O₂ to a final concentration of 0.3 mM with or without R1‑MVs at 10 µg mL⁻¹ or 30 µg mL⁻¹; incubate as required before harvesting.

steps.title: Extract proteins and run western blot
steps.instruction: Lyse cells for cytosolic proteins using RIPA buffer (Pierce) and for nuclear proteins using the CelLytic NuCLEAR Extraction Kit (Sigma‑Aldrich); measure protein concentration with BCA assay; separate 10 % SDS‑PAGE gels, transfer to PVDF membranes, block with 5 % skim milk; incubate primary antibodies (1:1000) overnight at 4 °C (anti‑Bcl‑2, anti‑Bax, anti‑cytochrome C, anti‑cleaved‑caspase‑3/8/9, anti‑PARP, anti‑p38, anti‑ERK, anti‑JNK, p‑ERK, p‑JNK, p‑p38, Nrf2, β‑actin, α‑tubulin); wash and incubate HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody (anti‑rabbit, 1:5000) for 1 h at room temperature; visualize with electrochemiluminescence advance kit (Millipore, Merck KGaA).

steps.title: Perform Annexin V/PI apoptosis assay
steps.instruction: Treat HaCaT cells with 30 µg mL⁻¹ R1‑MVs or ΔDR2577‑R1‑MVs for 12 h, then add H₂O₂ (0.3 mM) for another 12 h at 37 °C; harvest cells, stain with annexin V (1:50 in binding buffer, BD Bioscience) for 15 min at room temperature, wash, then stain with propidium iodide (1:25 in binding buffer) for 10 min at room temperature; analyze Annexin V‑positive, PI‑positive, and double‑positive populations using a FACSverse cytometer and FlowJo v10 software.

steps.title: Analyze data statistically
steps.instruction: Process experimental results with GraphPad Prism 7 (2018); apply Tukey’s multiple‑comparison test or an unpaired t‑test as appropriate; present data as mean ± SD; consider p < 0.05 statistically significant.
